Light Up a Life is coming round again, and I find I'm thinking about it more this year than usual. It will be seven years this month since my husband Ray died at the hospice, so this one is a little more personal than my usual notes. Please bear with me.

Memory tags go up on the counter in the shop from Monday 16 November. The suggested donation is £3, but please don't feel you have to pay anything to take one. If you'd rather write your tag at home, there are envelopes on the counter.

The first year I hung Ray's tag, I could barely write it. Now I write it at the counter, with the same pen. It still isn't easy, but it is a little easier each year. If you're finding it hard this year, you're not alone in that.

The tree is for anyone who is grieving, not only families who have been cared for by the hospice. Whoever you have lost, you're welcome to put their name on it. And if you'd simply like to come in and stand by the tree for a while, you're very welcome to do that too. There's no need to buy anything.

The lights will be switched on at 4pm on Saturday 28 November. The Gildencroft Primary choir is coming back to sing a few carols, and Doreen has promised her mince pies again.

Every name on the tags will be read out at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December at 3pm in the day centre. You don't need to come to the service for your loved one's name to be read.

Thank you to everyone who came in last year, who wrote names, who stood out in the cold to hear the children sing, and who has kept coming back to us. We had 412 names on the tree last year. Each one belongs to someone who mattered to somebody, and I'm grateful to have been trusted with every one of them.

Jean
